learn.hook: Can one little mango picture stand for 5 mangoes? In a pictograph, it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how many things one symbol stands for, like 🥭 = 5 mangoes.
To read it, multiply the number of symbols by the key.
Half a symbol stands for half the key number.
Choose a key that keeps the pictures easy to draw and count.

example.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎 and half an 🍎. How many apples?

learn.reallife: Pictographs are used in newspapers, school charts and posters to show data in a fun way.

items.text: Half a ☀️ stands for ___ sunny day

quiz.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples does the shop have?
quiz.mistake: Counts the symbols but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: ⭐ = 4 children. A row shows 3 and a half ⭐. How many children is that?
quiz.explain: 3 stars = 12 children. Half a star = 2 children. 12 + 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: 🏏 = 10 runs. Kabir has 🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏 and Joseph has 🏏🏏🏏. How many more runs did Kabir score?
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🙂 = 5 children. How many 🙂 are needed to show 35 children?
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph have a key?
options: So we know how many each symbol stands for
quiz.explain: Without the key we cannot tell if one symbol means 1, 5 or 10 things.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the symbols always mean 1 each

quiz.q: Key: 📚 = 20 books. The library row shows 📚📚 and half a 📚. How many books?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the half symbol

quiz.q: A pictograph will show 200, 350 and 500 visitors at a mela. Which key is the best choice?
quiz.explain: With 50, the rows need 4, 7 and 10 symbols. Easy to draw and read!
quiz.mistake: Picks a key that needs hundreds of symbols or does not divide the numbers

quiz.q: Key: 🌸 = 6 flowers. Meena picked 24 flowers. How many 🌸 symbols show this?
quiz.mistake: Uses the key number as the answer

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'In a pictograph, how do I know how many things one picture means?'
teach.praise: Yay! Read the key, then multiply the symbols by it. Easy-peasy!
teach.nudge: What part of the pictograph tells me what a symbol is worth? What do I do then?

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? A bar graph shows the winner in one look!
points: A bar graph uses bars of different lengths to show data.
The longer or taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
The scale on the side tells what each line stands for, like 1 line = 2 children.
All bars should be the same width with equal gaps between them.
Bars can go up (vertical) or across (horizontal).

example.q: On a bar graph each line stands for 2 children. The Mango bar reaches 6 lines. How many children chose mango?

learn.reallife: Cricket scorecards on TV, rainfall charts and school results often use bar graphs.

games.title: Fewest to most votes
games.prompt: Favourite game votes: Kabaddi 9, Cricket 15, Football 11, Kho-kho 6. Order the bars from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: In a bar graph, all bars should be the same width.
Only the length should change, so the graph is fair.
The longest bar shows the smallest number.
The longest bar shows the biggest number.
We need the scale to read the numbers on a bar graph.
The scale tells what each line stands for.
Bars can be drawn going across, not only up.
Horizontal bar graphs work the same way.
If 1 line = 5, a bar 4 lines tall shows 4.

quiz.q: Favourite fruits in Class 5: Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10. Which fruit has the tallest bar?
quiz.explain: Mango has the biggest number, 12, so its bar is tallest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the same fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8), how many more children chose Mango than Banana?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two bars

quiz.q: In the fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10), how many children voted in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one bar

quiz.q: On a bar graph, each line stands for 2 children. A bar reaches 7 lines. How many children does it show?
quiz.mistake: Reads the number of lines and forgets the scale

quiz.q: Runs in each over: Over 1 = 6, Over 2 = 10, Over 3 = 4, Over 4 = 12. Which over had the most runs?
quiz.explain: Over 4 has the tallest bar with 12 runs.
quiz.mistake: Picks the over with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the runs graph (6, 10, 4 and 12 runs), how many runs were scored in all 4 overs?
quiz.mistake: Makes an adding slip or misses one over

quiz.q: Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Which month had the fewest rainy days?
quiz.explain: September has the shortest bar, 6 days.
quiz.mistake: Picks the month with the most rain

quiz.q: What does a taller bar on a bar graph tell us?
options: There is more of that thing
There is less of that thing
quiz.explain: Bar height shows the number. Taller means more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the height has no meaning

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I read a bar graph?'
teach.praise: Super! Taller bars mean more, and the scale tells me the exact number!
teach.nudge: What does the height of a bar show? What tells me what each line is worth?

learn.hook: Class 5 did a survey: how do you come to school? Let's be data detectives and find the story in the numbers!
points: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5 (four lines and one across) to count quickly.
From data we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.
We can also find fractions of the data: 20 out of 40 is half.
Only say what the data really shows. Do not guess things it does not tell.

example.q: 40 children answered: 20 walk, 12 come by bus, 8 cycle. What fraction walk? How many more walk than cycle?
example.answer: Half walk; 12 more walk than cycle

learn.reallife: Schools, shops and doctors collect data to make good decisions.

games.title: Data: dogs 10, cats 6, fish 4
buckets: Can be answered from the data
items: How many more dogs than cats?
Which pet is the least common?

items.q: Bars of 12 and 7: how many more?

quiz.q: A tally shows two bundles of five and 3 more lines. What number is that?
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1

quiz.q: 40 children were asked how they come to school. 20 walk. What fraction of the children walk?
quiz.mistake: Writes the number who walk over the number who don't (20/20)

quiz.q: In the same survey, 20 children walk and 8 cycle. How many more walk than cycle?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Temperatures this week: Mon 30°, Tue 32°, Wed 29°, Thu 33°. Which day was the hottest?
quiz.explain: 33° is the highest, so Thursday was the hottest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the coolest day

quiz.q: Favourite part of Diwali: Sweets 15, Diyas 12, Rangoli 9, Lights 4. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Lights are more popular than Diyas
Rangoli and Diyas got the same votes
quiz.explain: 15 is the biggest number, so Sweets got the most votes.
quiz.mistake: Reads the numbers carelessly

quiz.q: In that Diwali survey (15, 12, 9 and 4 votes), how many children voted in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the smallest number

quiz.q: Books read this month: Riya 5, Arjun 8, Meena 6, Kabir 5. How many children read more than 5 books?
quiz.explain: Arjun (8) and Meena (6) read more than 5. Riya and Kabir read exactly 5, which is not more than 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts children who read exactly 5 as 'more than 5'

quiz.q: In a quiz, Team A scored 45 and Team B scored 60. By how many points did Team B win?
quiz.mistake: Adds the scores

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What can we learn from a table of numbers?'
teach.praise: Wow! Data tells us the most, the least, the total and how many more. I'm a data detective now!
teach.nudge: What questions can I answer from the numbers? Can I find the biggest and the total?
